headline: Antonelli charges from 19th on the grid to win in Monza
standfirst: Kimi Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 3.857s ahead of George Russell, with Max Verstappen completing the podium after 53 laps of Monza.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Pierre Gasly lined up first on the grid. Gasly converted that into the lead at the end of lap one. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Antonelli, up 5 places to 14th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 6 times. Laps led: Russell (40), Antonelli (9), Verstappen (3) and Gasly (1). Antonelli took the lead for good on lap 50. The race was neutralised by 1 red flag (lap 3) and 1 safety car period (lap 3).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Antonelli made 1 stop, running hard → medium tyres. The field made 9 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.4s for Hulkenberg on lap 27. 10 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Kimi Antonelli made up the most ground, climbing 18 places from 19th to 1st. Gasly went the other way, slipping from 1st to 7th. Timing recorded 334 on-track position changes, 25 of them by Antonelli.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Alonso (lap 24), Leclerc (lap 2) and Stroll (lap 27) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 52°C to 57°C, with air at 32–33°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:23.504 on lap 53.
